note: Hand-written steps, one action each. Every number must appear in a cited source (keys: vdata, cfg, convars, pros, news:<date>, fandom:<Page>, web:<id>, video:<topic>, guide = a step that only uses this guide's own pages). A step that cites a prose source (fandom:, news:, web:) must quote (q) the passage it relies on, word for word. A step that cites only videos is shown as advice from that video. [[Weapon]] must be a weapon card, `command` must be in the game's convar/command dump, {Map|Callout} must be on that map's callout map. build.py fails on any miss.

sections.title: How to get back into CS2 after a break
sections.need: You'll need: CS2 installed and about an hour for the first session.

steps.t: Open **What changed** in this guide and read the updates since you last played.
Check the Active Duty pool on **Maps**: Cache replaced Overpass when Premier Season Five began, and Anubis is back in.
q: Added Cache to the Active Duty Map Pool
Removed Overpass from the Active Duty Map Pool
Added Anubis to the Active Duty Map Pool

steps.t: Open **Settings** and the new **Crosshair/Scopes** tab: crosshair length and thickness are now set in pixels.
q: A new "Crosshair/Scopes" tab is available in the Settings menu
The new crosshair thickness and length units are in pixels

steps.t: Set your crosshair again with **How to set up your crosshair** (pro values are on the **Settings & crosshair** page).
Play one Deathmatch to warm up your aim and counter-strafing.
Pick two maps from the pool.
Learn three smokes for each of them on their map pages.
steps.note: Each map page also has the callouts on its radar.

steps.t: Queue Premier.
If your CS Rating is hidden, win 1 Premier match to show it again.
q: they must win 1 Premier match to show their CS rating

sections.check: You are done when your crosshair feels right, you know the seven pool maps and your CS Rating is visible.

sections.title: How to counter-strafe and shoot accurately
sections.need: You'll need: a private server for practice (see **Console commands**).

steps.t: Stop moving before every shot you want to land.
q: the faster or more movement is done, the more significant a weapon's bullet/pellet spread will be
steps.note: The faster you move, the wider your bullets spread. Each weapon card shows the moving and standing values under Accuracy.

steps.t: Strafe sideways with A (or D) to peek the angle.
The moment you see the enemy, release A and tap D once to cancel your speed.
Fire the first shot as soon as you stop.
Strafe back into cover after the shots.
Hold the walk key when you need to be quiet: walking lowers your footstep noise and keeps you more accurate.
q: use the specific walk key to slow down their movement, increasing their accuracy and reducing their footstep noise

steps.t: To practise, paste the practice block from **Console commands** on a private server.
Run `weapon_debug_spread_show 1` to see your spread shrink when you stop.
Run `cl_showpos 1` to see your speed on screen; with an [[AK-47]] your top speed is 215.

sections.check: It works when your first bullet hits the head while you are strafing between two boxes.

sections.title: How to control a spray
sections.need: You'll need: a private server with infinite ammo (see **Console commands**), and the pattern video for your rifle (below and on each rifle's card).

steps.t: Aim at head height before the fight, so you do not need to move your crosshair up.
Stand still and fire: your first bullet is not affected by recoil and lands near your crosshair.
q: The first shot fired while spraying is always unaffected by recoil, and will land near the crosshair's location, accounting for inaccuracy

steps.t: Keep firing and pull your mouse down as the spray climbs.
Move your mouse against the spray's sideways sway.
steps.note: Each rifle has its own pattern: the pattern video for your gun is further down this page.

steps.t: Practise on a wall: paste the practice block from **Console commands** on a private server.
Run `sv_showimpacts 1` to see where each bullet landed.
Compare your bullet holes with the pattern in the video for your gun.
If the enemy is far away, shoot short bursts and let the recoil reset between them.
q: When the player stops shooting, the recoil index will drop down and return to zero

steps.t: If a second enemy appears during a spray, keep pulling down while you move your aim to them (a spray transfer).

sections.check: It works when most of a spray at a wall lands inside a head-sized circle at close range.

sections.title: How to decide: buy, save or force
sections.need: You'll need: the team's money (hold the scoreboard key or open the buy menu during freeze time).

steps.t: Read your team's money during freeze time.
steps.note: Everyone starts the half with $800 and nobody can hold more than $16000.

steps.t: Full buy if every player can afford a rifle, Kevlar + Helmet and grenades (totals are on **Buy rounds**).
If most of the team cannot full buy, save: buy nothing (or only a pistol) so everyone can full buy together next round.
Count on the loss bonus: $1400 after one loss and $500 more for each further loss, up to $3400.
q: Round loss bonuses are based on the count of a team's round losses

steps.t: Remember the half starts with one loss already counted, so a lost pistol round pays $1900.
q: Losing pistol round $1900

steps.t: Expect a win to lower the loss count by one, not reset it (`mp_consecutive_loss_aversion` is 1 in the game files).
Win money is bigger: $3250 for a win by elimination, $3500 for a bomb explosion or a defuse.
Use kill rewards: $300 with most guns, $600 with most SMGs, $900 with a [[Nova]], [[MAG-7]] or [[Sawed-Off]], $100 with the [[AWP]] and $1500 with a knife.
If you are T, plant the bomb even in a lost round: the planter gets $300.
If you are CT, every T your team kills adds a $50 team award, win or lose.
q: Counter-Terrorists now receive a $50 team award for each Terrorist eliminated in a round

steps.t: Force buy (armor plus the best gun you can afford) when the enemy is saving or when your loss bonus is already at its top.

sections.check: It works when your team buys together and nobody is left with a pistol while four teammates have rifles.

sections.title: How to play the pistol round
sections.need: You'll need: $800 (everyone's money in round one).

steps.t: Buy a [[Kevlar Vest]] for $650, or skip it and buy a better pistol plus grenades.
If you skip armor, try a [[P250]] for $300 with a [[Flashbang]] for $200 and a [[Smoke Grenade]] for $300.
If you are CT, let one player buy a [[Defuse Kit]] for $400.
Stay close to a teammate so either of you can trade: kill the enemy who just killed the other.
Stop moving before each shot (see **How to counter-strafe**).
If you win, buy SMGs or upgraded pistols next round: SMG kills pay $600.
If you lose, agree a plan for round two with the team before round one ends.
q: Losing pistol round $1900
steps.note: A lost pistol round pays $1900 each: the plan is to save or to buy only cheap items.

sections.check: It works when the whole team made the same plan for round two before round one ended.

sections.title: How to learn and throw lineups
sections.need: You'll need: the map's page in this guide and a private server.

steps.t: Open the map's page and pick three lineups from **Lineups** (each one jumps to its spot in the video).
Start a private server on that map and paste the practice block from **Console commands**.
Run `sv_grenade_trajectory_prac_pipreview 1` to see where a grenade will land before you throw.
Stand exactly where the video stands and put your crosshair on the same spot.
Throw with the same method as the video (left click, right click, both, or jump-throw).
Run `sv_rethrow_last_grenade` to repeat the throw until it lands every time.
Buy grenades with the limit in mind: 4 grenades at most, and at most 2 of them flashbangs.
Use a [[Smoke Grenade]] to put out an enemy [[Molotov]] or [[Incendiary Grenade]] fire.
q: The flames can be extinguished by a Smoke Grenade

sections.check: It works when you land each of your three lineups first try in a real match.

sections.title: How to set up your crosshair
sections.need: You'll need: the **Settings & crosshair** page of this guide open.

steps.t: Open the **Crosshair/Scopes** tab in **Settings**.
q: A new "Crosshair/Scopes" tab is available in the Settings menu

steps.t: Choose a style.
steps.note: The table on **Settings & crosshair** shows which styles the pros use most.

steps.t: Set length, thickness and gap in pixels: a 1-pixel crosshair with 8-pixel bars and a 4-pixel gap is thickness 1, length 8, gap 4.
q: if you want a 1-pixel wide crosshair with a bar length of 8 pixels and a gap of 4 pixels, then you would set: thickness = 1, length = 8, and gap = 4

steps.t: Or type the same values in the console, for example `cl_crosshair_length 2`, `cl_crosshair_thickness 1` and `cl_crosshair_gap 1`.
If someone gives you a share code, paste it into the share-code field in the crosshair settings.
q: They can be applied through the settings or via the command apply_crosshair_code
steps.note: The wiki also names the console command `apply_crosshair_code`, but the game's own command list flags it developmentonly, so it may not work outside a test build.

steps.t: If you change resolution later, leave the values alone: the game rescales the pixels for you.
q: the new crosshair system automatically rescales pixel counts when the display resolution changes

steps.t: Look at it on a bright wall and on a dark wall in a match.
If it disappears on either wall, change its colour.

sections.check: It works when you can see the centre of your crosshair on every map without looking for it.

sections.title: How to set sensitivity and video like the pros
sections.need: You'll need: your mouse software (for DPI) and the **Settings & crosshair** page.

steps.t: Set your mouse to 400 or 800 DPI, the two most common values in the pro list.
Pick an in-game sensitivity so DPI x sensitivity (eDPI) is near the pro median of 800.
steps.note: If you are new to low sensitivity, move toward it in small steps.

steps.t: Leave zoom sensitivity at 1 unless your scoped aim feels wrong; 1 is the median.
Choose a resolution: most listed pros play 4:3 stretched.
steps.note: If 4:3 feels cramped, 16:9 native is a normal choice too.

steps.t: Turn on **Boost Player Contrast**, like most of the pros with full settings.
Turn off **V-Sync**, like most of the pros with full settings.
Set **Radar Map Zoom** lower to see more of the map; the pro values are listed on the settings page.

sections.check: It works when you can turn fully around with one comfortable arm swipe and still hit small flicks.

sections.title: How to peek and hold angles
sections.need: You'll need: one teammate to trade you, or bots on a private server.

steps.t: Hold an angle from further back, so the enemy must swing wider before they can see you.
Keep your crosshair at head height on the edge where the enemy will appear.
If you want information without a fight, shoulder-peek: show only your shoulder and step back at once.
If you want the fight, wide-peek (swing far past the corner in one move) with a counter-strafe and shoot first.
Clear angles one at a time: move to the next only after the first is safe.
Swing together with a teammate so the enemy can only shoot one of you.

sections.check: It works when you lose fewer fights to players you had already seen.

sections.title: How to play after the bomb is planted
sections.need: You'll need: a plan for which side of the site you will hold.

steps.t: As T, count down from 40: the bomb explodes 40 seconds after the plant.
q: 40 seconds under a competitive ruleset

steps.t: As T, hold the bomb from different angles so a defuser can be shot from two places.
As T, save a [[Molotov]] to throw on the bomb when you hear the defuse start.
As CT, buy a [[Defuse Kit]] in every buy round: it cuts the defuse from 10 seconds to 5.
q: The time it takes to defuse C4 is 10 seconds or 5 seconds with a defuse kit

steps.t: As CT, wait for teammates and retake the site together instead of one at a time.
When the bomb is about to blow, get behind a wall or round a corner: since Season Five the blast is a shockwave that fades around corners and does not go through walls.
q: the shockwave dissipates around corners and doesn't go through walls

steps.t: Check your health bar before the blast: it flashes a preview of how much the explosion will hurt you where you stand.
q: check your health bar which will flash a preview of how well you'll fare after the blast

sections.check: It works when you know before the plant who holds which angle, and nobody dies to the blast after a lost round.

sections.title: How to get and climb a CS Rating in Premier
sections.need: You'll need: Prime Status and profile rank 10.

steps.t: Unlock Premier with a Prime Status account at profile rank 10.
q: players need to have a Prime Status account and a minimum profile rank

steps.t: Win 10 Premier matches to reveal your CS Rating.
q: The player has to win 10 Premier matches before their CS rating is shown

steps.t: Pick maps you know: Team 1 picks one map, Team 2 picks two, Team 1 picks a final map, and one of the four is chosen at random.
q: Team 1 picks one map Team 2 picks two maps Team 1 picks a final map
a single map will be randomly selected

steps.t: Plan for 24 rounds (12 per half); a tie after that goes to one overtime of 3 rounds per half.
steps.note: The wiki says both teams get $10000 at the start of each overtime half. The game's default for `mp_overtime_startmoney` is the same, but the Premier server setting is not in the pulled game files, so treat the amount as the wiki's.
q: If both teams tie their score after 24 rounds, only one overtime period is played out
Both teams are given $10,000 at the start of their overtime half

steps.t: If it is still tied 15-15 after overtime, the match ends in a draw.
q: If both teams are still tied 15-15 after overtime has finished then the Premier match ends in a tie

steps.t: Expect a promotion match when one win would take you over a 5000 line; your rating shows as X,999 in it.
q: If the player's CS Rating can increase to reach a 5000 CS Rating interval from the current match being won then the next Premier Match will be a "Promotion

steps.t: Keep playing Premier: a rating hides after a time without Premier matches.
q: inactivity if they stop playing Premier
they must win 1 Premier match to show their CS rating
steps.note: If it hides, win 1 match to show it again.

sections.check: Your rating colour band is shown on **Ranks**.

summary.t: Needs Prime Status and profile rank 10; win 10 matches to show your rating.
q: players need to have a Prime Status account and a minimum profile rank
The player has to win 10 Premier matches before their CS rating is shown

summary.t: Map pick: Team 1 picks one, Team 2 picks two, Team 1 picks one; one of the four is played at random.
q: Team 1 picks one map Team 2 picks two maps Team 1 picks a final map
a single map will be randomly selected

summary.t: 24 rounds; a tie goes to one overtime of 3 rounds per half (the wiki gives each team $10000 per overtime half). Still tied at 15-15 after it: the match is a draw.
q: If both teams tie their score after 24 rounds, only one overtime period is played out
Both teams are given $10,000 at the start of their overtime half
If both teams are still tied 15-15 after overtime has finished then the Premier match ends in a tie

summary.t: Ratings hide after inactivity; win 1 match to show it again.
q: inactivity if they stop playing Premier
they must win 1 Premier match to show their CS rating

sections.title: How to run a practice session
sections.need: You'll need: the practice server commands from **Console commands**.

steps.t: Warm up in one Deathmatch, shooting only after a counter-strafe.
Start a private server on the map you play next.
Paste the practice block from **Console commands** into the console.
Spray at a wall with `sv_showimpacts 1` until the [[AK-47]] or [[M4A1-S]] spray stays tight.
Add a bot with `bot_add_t`.
steps.note: The practice block removes all bots with `bot_kick`, so the server is empty while you spray at the wall; this adds back one target to aim at.

steps.t: Freeze the bots with `bot_stop 1`.
Counter-strafe each time you peek a bot.
Throw your map's lineups with `sv_rethrow_last_grenade` until each lands first try.
Open one of your lost matches in the demo viewer with `demoui`.
Write down one mistake to fix next match.

sections.check: It works when you finish with one concrete thing to try in your next match.
